body:
3.7.1  Verify the application ensures a valid login session or requires re-authentication or secondary verification   before allowing any sensitive transactions or account modifications.


E.g. user logged in with login and password and got session token that stored in cookies.
He tries to perform any actions - create / update / delete object OR change his account settings.

I see two ways according to this requirement:
1st. session token is verified (e.g. search in db that such token exists)  
if session token is not correct (not found in DB) - action is not performed
OR
2d. user is asked to enter correct password for sensitive operations and changes of his account

QUESTIONS:
1. Does this requirement approve either 1st or 2d way of implementation
2. In 1st variant ehat is the next step if incorrect session token detected  - block IP , nothing?
3. In 2d variant - what does it mean sensitive transactions - can it be administrative actions ?
4. If yes seems ASVS has another requirement about it:
.4.3.1  Verify administrative interfaces   use appropriate multi-factor authentication to prevent unauthorized use.
Is it about the same or 3.7.1 includes 4.3.1 but it's wider?

Thank you

comments.body: Hi @belalena, before I dig into this, please can you confirm you read [this explanatory text](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x12-V3-Session-management.md#description-of-the-half-open-attack) at the start of 3.7
@belalena I'll look into if we can make 3.7.1 easier to understand, but if you could please answer Josh's question, that would be helpful in addressing your issue.

Sorry to quibble @jmanico but I think this might be quite a significant change. Whereas the previous wording allowed for the existance of a valid logged in session to be sufficient (to avoid a half-open attack), this new wording (for an L1 control) unequivocally requires re-authentication or secondary factor verification for "sensitive" functions.

Are you sure we should mandate that for L1? Do you think that change is too big for 4.0.2?

I prefer this for 4.0.2 and think L2 is better :)

You are not quibbling, this is significant, and you are welcome.

:) Jim

 verification for L2.

Either way, I really think that the changes we are proposing change the meaning of the original requirement so need to wait for 4.1
